title: The former Enron office complex, Houston, at night
description: Night view of the office towers in downtown Houston that the Commons file page identifies as the Enron complex. Photographed in March 2008, several years after Enron's collapse.
alt: Two curved glass office towers lit up at night, joined by a curved walkway, with a Smith Street sign in the foreground.
author: Alex (Flickr user; originally posted to Flickr as "Enron Complex")
credit_line: Photo: Alex, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0
notes: License confirmed by Flickr review bot on Commons (Aug 2008). Downloaded as 1280px Commons thumbnail.

title: Enron corporate logo
description: Enron's tilted-E logo. Commons gives its source as Enron's 2000 annual report (archived copy) and names the designer as Paul Rand.
alt: Enron logo: a tilted capital E in blue, green and red above the word Enron.
author: Paul Rand (designer), per Wikimedia Commons
license: Public domain (text logo below the threshold of originality; may still be a trademark)
credit_line: Enron logo, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain text logo; trademark)
notes: Commons marks it PD-textlogo and 'trademarked'. Use it only to identify the company, not in a way that suggests endorsement. The date in the file name (1997) comes from Commons, not from the library; do not cite it as a fact. The 1986 logo on Commons is CC BY-SA 4.0 (a redrawing) and was not taken.

title: A natural gas pipeline station
description: Above-ground pipes and valves at a small natural gas pipeline station on a university campus in Ohio (2020). A generic picture of gas pipeline equipment; not an Enron facility.
alt: Dark painted gas pipes, valves and meters rising out of a concrete pad inside a fenced enclosure.
author: Mbrickn
credit_line: Photo: Mbrickn, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0
notes: Modest image; caption must say it is generic, not Enron's. Downloaded as 1280px Commons thumbnail.

title: A trading floor: the New York Stock Exchange
description: The trading floor of the New York Stock Exchange, photographed by Carol M. Highsmith (Library of Congress; dated only 'between 1980 and 2006'). Shown as a generic example of a trading floor. It is a stock exchange, not Enron's energy-trading floor.
alt: A crowded stock exchange floor seen from above, with trading booths full of screens and large NYSE banners hanging from the ceiling.
author: Carol M. Highsmith (Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LCCN 2011632435)
license: Public domain (Highsmith gift to the Library of Congress; LoC: "No known restrictions on publication")
credit_line: Photo: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress (public domain)
notes: Traders visible are not identified; do not describe any individual. LoC rights advisory read from loc.gov JSON record. Downloaded as 960px Commons thumbnail (portrait).

title: Senate Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on Enron, January 2002
description: Photo caption from the source (Senator Fred Thompson's office): Senator Thompson questions former SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt during the Governmental Affairs Committee's opening hearing into the Enron bankruptcy. Seated from left to right are Senators Susan Collins (R-ME), Senator Thompson, and Joe Lieberman (D-CT). Dated 2002-01-24 on Commons.
alt: Three senators seated at a hearing dais with microphones and name plates; the man in the center is speaking.
author: Office of Senator Fred Thompson (archived at webarchive.loc.gov)
license: Public domain (work of the U.S. Congress)
credit_line: Photo: Office of Sen. Fred Thompson, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
notes: Only Collins, Thompson and Lieberman are named by the source; staff behind them are not identified. Levitt is not visible. The hearing date comes from the photo caption, not the library; writers should cite a library document for any claim about the hearing. Small original (510px wide); saved as 500px thumbnail, so display it no wider than ~500px.

title: Enron's former buildings in downtown Houston, 2009
description: The curved sky bridge linking Enron's former office towers in downtown Houston, photographed in June 2009, after the company's collapse.
alt: A curved glass sky bridge crossing a downtown street between tall glass office buildings, with parked vans below.
author: Chanilim714 (Panoramio)
credit_line: Photo: Chanilim714, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
notes: Share-alike: if the site alters (e.g. crops) this photo, the altered version must also be CC BY-SA 3.0. License confirmed by Panoramio review bot on Commons (Oct 2016). Downloaded as 960px Commons thumbnail.

title: Signing of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, July 30, 2002
description: White House caption: President George W. Bush shakes hands with Congressman Mike Oxley, R-OH, during the signing ceremony of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act in the East Room, July 30 (2002). Photo by Eric Draper, White House Photo Office.
alt: President Bush shaking hands with Congressman Oxley in the White House East Room, with other men in suits nearby and a podium sign reading Corporate Responsibility.
author: Eric Draper, White House Photo Office (The Bush White House)
license: Public domain (work of the Executive Office of the President)
credit_line: White House photo by Eric Draper, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
notes: Source identifies only Bush and Oxley; the other people are not named, so do not name them. The Commons caption also contains a Bush quotation; do not use it unless it is verified against a library document (e.g. the signing remarks in the library). The signing date must be cited to a library document in the text. Small original (515px); saved as 500px thumbnail. Original White House page: https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/news/releases/2002/07/images/20020730_p20314-27a-ed-515h.html (not visited).

title: How a special purpose entity (SPE) works
description: Original diagram. Generic concept, not a specific Enron deal: a company moves an asset into a separate entity funded by outside lenders and investors, receives cash, and (if the rules treat the entity as truly independent) keeps the asset and the debt off its balance sheet.
alt: Diagram: the company sends an asset to a special purpose entity; outside investors and lenders fund the SPE; the SPE pays the company cash. A dashed box marks what stays on the company's balance sheet and what moves off it.
author: Ask Why site team (Image Researcher & Diagrammer agent)
notes: Wide version (800x560) for desktop/projector; narrow version (520x1010) for phones: use . Colors follow the OS light/dark setting when used as ; when inlined, the site can override with --diagram-bg, --diagram-ink, --diagram-muted. Each diagram carries its own background panel so it stays legible if the manual theme toggle disagrees with the OS setting.

title: Illustration: waiting for the cash vs. mark-to-market
description: Original illustration with made-up numbers: a 10-year contract expected to earn $10 a year. Reporting profit as the cash is earned shows $10 each year; mark-to-market reports about $70 (the estimated present value of all ten years) in year 1 and only small updates afterwards. The cash received is the same either way.
alt: Two bar charts. Top: ten equal blue bars of $10, one per year. Bottom: one tall orange bar of about $70 in year 1, then nine tiny bars. Marked ILLUSTRATION.
author: Ask Why site team (Image Researcher & Diagrammer agent)
credit_line: Illustration: Ask Why site team (made-up numbers)
notes: 'About $70' = $10 a year for 10 years discounted at roughly 7% a year (present value ~ $70.24); the discount rate is not shown, to keep it simple. Same wide/narrow and theming notes as diagram-spe-basic.
